title: Decorators with wrapt
description: Guided JupyterLab workshops on writing decorators with wrapt: the wrapper signature, methods, arguments, state, and the decorators wrapt bundles, each beside the standard library version it replaces.

workshops.name: your-first-wrapt-decorator
workshops.title: Your first wrapt decorator
workshops.description: Write the four argument wrapper that wrapt turns into a decorator, beside the closure version with functools.wraps. Ask the decorated function about itself and get the right answers with nothing copied, then see what the decorated name really is, and meet the instance argument.

workshops.name: what-instance-tells-you
workshops.title: What instance tells you
workshops.description: One decorator on a plain function, an instance method, a class method, a static method and a class. Read what instance holds for each, see why args never contains self and why a call through the class looks the same, and learn the one ordering rule for classmethod.

workshops.name: arguments-to-the-decorator
workshops.title: Arguments to the decorator
workshops.description: Give a wrapt decorator settings of its own, three ways, each beside the standard library shape it replaces. A function that takes the settings and returns the decorator, a class whose __call__ is the wrapper, and a decorator that works with and without parentheses through wrapt.partial.

workshops.name: handling-the-arguments
workshops.title: Handling the arguments
workshops.description: What a wrapper does with the call's arguments. Why wrapt hands them over as a tuple and a dict rather than binding them to names, why args[0] is wrong, how a nested function binds the one argument you care about, how inspect.signature binds all of them by name with no special case for methods, and what a wrapper can do with the return value.
